I used live in house in Japan that was built over a farm field. I'm pretty sure it was a rice paddy farm.

The soil, not much was scraped when they but the house and only an inch or two of top soil (better than where I live now because it's just sod and no top soil).

The previous owners raised the garden and boxed it with railroad ties so I was slightly ahead of the game.

Since the soil was already nutrient dead I just dug it all up and dug a good 2-3 feet down into the clay; by hand. I then filled each grave sized hole with about 2 feet of trimmings from the shrubs, trees, leaves, grass and weeds. If I had any paper shreds I'd throw them along with raw food left overs from veggies and fruit.

I did almost 2 full car parking areas like this.

I couldn't get to a sand layer in the clay so drainage probably wasn't good but with all that carbon in there and depth really had a chance to decompose.

How did it turn out?

Lol, I moved back to the U.S. before I could really find out but when I dug new sections I'd cut into older areas and it looked great. I'd also rotate out some of the darker earth for areas that supplied my front garden areas.

I was on a 5-6 year plan ... Oh well
